help.editAndRunJVMAssemblyLanguageJALCod: Edit and run JVM Assembly Language (JAL) code.
help.langjal.description: JAL is an assembly language for writing JVM instructions as text. Read the LangJAL documentation for syntax and instructions, then edit and run code in the Jaspera sandbox.
help.langjal.title: About LangJAL

help.licenses.title: Open-source licenses
help.manual.debug.breakpoints: Click between a line number and its offset to set a breakpoint. Run pauses immediately before that instruction.
help.manual.debug.callerFrames: Select a caller frame to inspect its values at the call. The executing instruction is highlighted in the source. Native methods cannot be stepped into.
help.manual.debug.stepping: {kbd}F8{/kbd} resumes, {kbd}F10{/kbd} steps over, {kbd}F11{/kbd} enters a call, and {kbd}Shift{/kbd} + {kbd}F11{/kbd} steps out. The floating controls provide the same actions. Stop ends execution.
help.manual.debug.values: Current shows the paused state; After shows the next instruction’s effect. Unknown results are represented by their type or an unknown value. Unchanged values appear in one column.
help.manual.editor.completion: Type an instruction to see completions. Fields and methods are also suggested after {code}getstatic{/code} and {code}invokestatic{/code}.
help.manual.editor.errors: Hover an underline to read a diagnostic, or select it in Problems to jump to the source. Press {kbd}Ctrl{/kbd} + {kbd}.{/kbd} for available quick fixes.
help.manual.editor.formatting: Format with {kbd}Shift{/kbd} + {kbd}Alt{/kbd} + {kbd}F{/kbd}. Labels align with the method declaration, one level outside instructions.
help.manual.editor.offsets: The numbers beside line numbers are bytecode offsets from the start of each method. They update without a build. Encoding changes during compilation can affect the final offsets.
help.manual.files.entryFile: Choose the entry file in project properties. New projects default to {code}src/Main.jal{/code}.
help.manual.files.externalChanges: External changes are checked roughly once a second. If they conflict with unsaved edits, your edits are kept and a notice is shown.
help.manual.files.openFolder: Choose {strong}File → Open folder…{/strong} to work with multiple sources. Properties belong in {code}.jalprj{/code}; sources remain separate files such as {code}src/Main.jal{/code}. Folders without project properties also work. Opening a {code}.jalprj{/code} asks you to select its source folder.
help.manual.files.save: Save also preserves tab and window layouts; edits to {code}example{/code} are excluded. Use ZIP export if the browser cannot write directly to a folder.
help.manual.graph.connections: Use the checkboxes to show stack, local-variable, control-flow and exception connections. Hide connections you do not need.
help.manual.graph.exceptions: Instructions are grouped into blocks. Exception connections lead from protected regions to handlers; exceptions sharing a route use one connection.
help.manual.graph.loading: Graph displays every method in the current class. Method outlines appear first; instructions and connections appear as analysis finishes.
help.manual.graph.navigation: Click an instruction to jump to its source. Drag the background to pan; use the wheel to zoom.
help.manual.instructions.analysis: Editor hovers use source analysis. Use Debug to inspect values while execution is paused.
help.manual.instructions.browse: Instructions explains each instruction and includes examples. Click the search box to browse categories. Selecting an instruction closes the list. Clicking an instruction in the editor also opens its explanation.
help.manual.instructions.frames: Hover an instruction in an example to inspect the frame before and after it. TOP marks the top of the stack. Consumed values are red; added values are green. Locals appear when the instruction changes them.
help.manual.layout.detach: Release a tab outside the window, or choose Open in separate window from its context menu, to detach it. Instructions, Graph and other panels can move too. Empty child windows close automatically.
help.manual.layout.moveTabs: Hold a tab briefly, then drag it to another group. Files in Project can also be dropped into a group.
help.manual.layout.resize: Hover a tab to reveal its close button. {kbd}Alt{/kbd}-click closes the other tabs in that group. Drag group boundaries to resize.
help.manual.layout.theme: Choose {strong}View → Theme…{/strong} to change colors and panel styling. The browser remembers your selection.
help.manual.navigation.classFiles: Open a {code}.class{/code} through {strong}File → Open…{/strong} or drag it into the window. No project is required. Save the JAL with {strong}File → Export JAL…{/strong}.
help.manual.navigation.definitions: Hold {kbd}Ctrl{/kbd} and click a class or member, or press {kbd}F12{/kbd}, to open its definition. OpenJDK classes are disassembled into JAL. {kbd}Shift{/kbd}-click a label to visit its definition or uses.
help.manual.navigation.search: Press {kbd}Shift{/kbd} twice to search files, classes and members. Enter part of a name and select a result.
help.manual.offline.prepare: While connected, open {strong}Help → Prepare for offline use…{/strong}, check the storage requirement and press Save. After completion, the same URL works offline.
help.manual.offline.reset: Repeat preparation if you clear site data.
help.manual.offline.sources: This stores the editor and Java runtime. Save your sources separately through File.
help.manual.shortcuts.useTheShortcutsBel: Use the shortcuts below. On macOS, use {kbd}⌘{/kbd} instead of {kbd}Ctrl{/kbd}.
help.manual.start.breakpoints: Click between the line number and bytecode offset to remove the breakpoint. Without breakpoints, execution continues to the end.
help.manual.start.examples: The {code}example{/code} folder contains arithmetic, branches, loops and arrays. Try changing the code. Reloading resets these examples; use {strong}File → Export JAL…{/strong} to keep a copy.
help.manual.start.intro: Hello World opens on startup. Press {strong}Run{/strong} at the top right. Its preset breakpoint pauses before {code}invokevirtual{/code}; Debug shows the output stream and greeting on the stack. Press {kbd}F8{/kbd} to resume and print the greeting in Console.
